name: SDN Host Schema-Typed Record Write Node
description: Host storage.write connector (typed contracts 1.0): the SCHEMA-TYPED single-record write lane. Method "write_record" takes ONE SDS record on "record" (typed $IRM, the record the in-repo flows write), sends it as an SDS $PIV storage.write hostcall (StorageWriteParams SCHEMA + raw "data", answered with StorageWriteResult CID) and emits ONE $PNM on "result" (CID, FILE_NAME = the standard it was filed under). No JSON and no base64; the JSON lane's optional {source,type} meta port is gone: the type is the record frame's own type reference, and storage.write takes no source (the host attributes the write to the module). WHY IT EXISTS: mod-cell-tower-ingest-flow shipped a chunked bulk-ingest flow whose resume mark had nowhere durable to go, and all three candidate lanes were ruled out by measurement - hostcap/flatsql-store is wasi-threads (the flow compiler refuses to link it into a single-thread flow at all) and its records port admits only $OMM/$OCM/$OBD; hostcap/file fits but the Go server host has no filesystem capability handler, so it fails closed on the target box; storage.write was exactly right but schema-typed, and using it meant inventing an SDS record for a bookkeeping row, which is Themis's call. Themis ruled: $IRM was minted and ratified in spacedatastandards.org 1.196.0, so this node was built - and built GENERICALLY. Nothing here knows what $IRM is; any flow with a schema-typed row to persist gets a durable write lane out of this node and the existing storage_write grant, with ZERO Go host changes. THE TYPE AND THE BYTES MUST AGREE: storage.write files bytes under whatever type it is told, so a frame typed OMM over a buffer whose file identifier is $IRM would write a mark into the orbit table where it is indistinguishable from a corrupt element set and where nothing will look for it again. When the frame's declared type and the record's intrinsic file identifier disagree, the write is REFUSED - neither value is preferred and neither is coerced. Policy is the host's: storage.write is gated by the dedicated storage_write grant, which storage_query explicitly does NOT imply. RUNTIME TARGETS ARE [wasmedge] AND THAT IS THE TRUTHFUL DECLARATION, not a narrowing for convenience: storage_write is in the SDK's browser-incompatible capability set because a browser has no node store to write to, so declaring browser here would claim a lane that cannot exist. A flow that links this node is a server-side lane by construction.

externalInterfaces.description: Schema-typed single-record write through the host storage.write hostcall, sent as an SDS $PIV invocation (StorageWriteParams + raw data -> StorageWriteResult CID).

acceptedTypeSets.description: ONE $IRM (Ingest Resume Mark) record, a FlatBuffer root buffer. Its file identifier (bytes 4..7) must agree with the frame's type.

inputPorts.description: ONE SDS record to persist. A typed port names one standard: $IRM, the record cellular-network-ingest and terrain-ingest write here. Another standard is another manifest entry, not a code change.

acceptedTypeSets.description: $PNM (Publish Notification Message): CID = the content id the host assigned the record; FILE_NAME = the standard it was filed under, e.g. "IRM.fbs".

outputPorts.description: ONE $PNM per written record: CID and FILE_NAME (the standard).

methods.description: Persists ONE schema-typed SDS record through the policy-mediated storage.write hostcall (typed: SDS $PIV) and emits the content id the host assigned, as a $PNM. The node makes no policy decision: it moves bytes and refuses contradictions. A record whose frame type disagrees with its own file identifier is refused with error code "record-type-disagreement"; a record with neither is refused with "missing-record-type", because a write filed under a guessed type is a write nothing will ever find. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). write_record persists ONE record and answers with ONE cid, so a surplus cannot be merged into a correct answer - a second record silently dropped is a mark that was never durable, which is the exact failure this lane exists to fix. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames".

sequentialJustification.detail: Each record becomes one storage.write hostcall answered on the calling thread; the host runs independent invocations in parallel and this module creates no threads.
